$comment: The home's four carousels as a small film production (krizaka-internal#2450): one look across every shot (night or golden-hour Montréal, warm lamp light, brick, blue ink, the feather pen, film grain, the birds as the brand's characters), the founder's published reels as the source. Each shot is cut from its reel on one continuous take (a cut inside a take is not expanded by the model), then expanded to 16:9 by Runway Aleph 2.0 (video to video, targetAspectRatio 16:9) with the shared look prompt plus the shot's own. The phone plays the original vertical cut, so nothing is invented there. Re-run: node scripts/home-showcase.mjs render <shot|carousel> --env-file <env>; then upload with scripts/cdn-assets.mjs. Takes and costs: content/films/home-showcase.log.json. Titles on the image are the reels' own words, already published on @krizakahq; no new claim is written on a picture. Besides the reels' shots, each carousel holds clips already in 16:9 (« clips »): the brand film, what Sovkora generated for the blog, and the company media library (public use waits on the founder's annex B, flagged « library »). Their phone rendition is a 4:5 crop placed on the subject (« focus », 0 = left, 0.5 = centre).
look: Expand the frame to a wide cinematic 16:9 shot. Continue the scene naturally on both sides with the same light, palette, lens, depth of field and 35 mm film grain: Montréal, dark and warm, lamp light or blue hour, real textures. Keep everything already in the frame exactly as it is, including the centred title text and the small mono line at the top. Add no new text, no logo, no sign, no screen, no face, no person.

stills.$comment: A product in conception shows one still, not a carousel (founder, 2026-11-06, krizaka-internal#2802): a mood photo of the job it will do, never an app screen, in the carousels' look. Made locally with FLUX.2 [klein] 4B through mflux on the Mac's GPU (the engine of the blog's image series), under heavy-lock.sh, no paid run: mflux-generate-flux2 --model flux2-klein-4b --quantize 8 --steps 4 --width 1280 --height 720 --seed <seed> --prompt <prompt>. Then the carousels' grade (warm lamp light, blue-hour shadows kept, soft S-curve, light vignette, a film frame's softness, 35 mm grain) and the posters' encode (ffmpeg -q:v 4), uploaded with scripts/cdn-assets.mjs under home/showcase/<product>/<id>-wide.jpg. Each take was looked at in full size for a logo, a screen, readable text or a broken hand.

kridoc.idea: Mireille, who runs a neighbourhood hardware store in Montréal, pulls the sheet she was looking for from her filing cabinet, at blue hour
kridoc.prompt: Cinematic 35 mm film still, wide 16:9 frame, shallow depth of field, soft film grain, natural candid documentary photography. Montreal, evening, dark and warm: the warm light of one lamp, deep blue shadows from a window at blue hour, real textures, red brick, old wood. No text, no readable writing, no logo, no sign, no screen visible. In the back office of a small family hardware store in Montreal, a woman in her forties with curly dark hair and reading glasses pushed up on her head, wearing a denim work shirt, pulls one folder out of an open drawer of an old wooden filing cabinet and looks at it with a quiet smile of relief. Shelves of cardboard archive boxes and binders behind her, a brick wall, a window at blue hour.
